_about: The machine-readable half of this project's work record, so 'what is open' stops being prose
that drifts. tests/test_status.py grades it in CI; the operator's own status renderer merges
it with the items that are not publishable.
Why it exists: a review of this project's own notes on 2026-09-28 found three items describing
their work as 'BUILT, unshipped (commit a4722fb, not pushed; no release cut)' for a change that
had shipped in 1.0.37. Nothing was lying on purpose - the record was prose, and prose has no
way to disagree with the repository. So every item here carries an anchor git can check.
state:  open | blocked | wish | shipped | closed
anchor: {file: <path>}                      the work is a gap in this file
{commit: <sha>, expect: tagged}     must be reachable from a tag (it shipped)
{commit: <sha>, expect: untagged}   must be reachable from NO tag (it has not)
gate:   what would close it, so the next reader knows what 'done' looks like

items.title: the Linux installer has no --install-python
items.detail: The macOS installer takes the flag; the Linux script and the Windows one never mention it. A per-host gap rather than a bug: the flag exists so a host can point the install at an interpreter it already trusts.
items.gate: the flag in install/install-tinycmdr.sh, or a decision that Linux does not need it

items.title: the Linux installer assumes apt and detects no distro
items.detail: Its one package call is a bare 'apt-get install -y -q python3-venv' behind an ensurepip probe, and the error text names apt. On a non-apt distribution ensurepip may be absent from the system Python, so that branch fires and the package manager does not exist. The install has been done by hand on a non-apt host, so the path is survivable, but no CI job exercises one.
items.gate: a distro branch, or a documented 'supported: Debian-shaped' with the failure named

items.title: the Windows CI job runs few suites and none that touch the platform switches
items.detail: The job selects a deliberately small set - the ones known to pass on Windows - while several suites branch on IS_WINDOWS for exactly the platform-specific behaviour that goes untested there. A suite that cannot run on a runner exits 77, which the gate counts as red, so widening it is a sequence of small additions rather than one.
items.gate: the IS_WINDOWS-branching suites added to the Windows job, one at a time

items.title: tools/* is gitignored, so tool code that was built and smoke-tested ships nowhere
items.detail: tools/ is per-host by design and only four files ship (README.md, patch.py, process.py, toolsmith.py). A full GUI-driving tool was written, tested on three platforms and left out of every archive: tools/README.md is tracked while the tools it documents are not.
items.gate: a policy: version them, or state in the README that tools/ is per-host by design

items.title: eval sampling is inherited, so two arms of the same build are not comparable
items.detail: The baseline file says it out loud: two arms of the same build differed by 36% of steps and 14% of tokens. The harness has a sampling key set and a per-model profile path, but the profile covers output caps only, so it cannot express sampling or generation length - the two things that move most between runs and matter most on a small model.
items.gate: the sampling set pinned for eval arms and surfaced in the startup line

items.title: the 'built for weak local models' claim has no small-model measurement
items.detail: No eval arm has run against a small window or a small model - every number in the baseline came from a large budget against one endpoint. That is the differentiator the README advertises and the one claim without evidence behind it.
items.gate: two arms - same build, a small model on a small window, sampling pinned - scored against the graded set

items.title: output caps come from a model-name match, not the detected window
items.detail: The per-model profile keys caps off a substring of the model name while the window-detection routes already know the real window. A new or unnamed model - the common case for someone swapping quantisations - gets the desktop defaults.
items.gate: caps derived from the detected window, plus a few named small-context profiles in config.example.json

items.title: search egress is gated and the provider chain is configurable
items.detail: Shipped in 1.0.37. The gate defaults to allowing off-LAN search, which was the direction the shipped installers ask about.

items.title: a tool can show the model the screen, and the image rides one request
items.detail: Shipped in 1.0.38. Dormant unless the vision flag is on; capped at two images of 4 MB per request.

items.title: a *_PASSWORD environment variable is a credential at 6 characters, not 12
items.detail: Shipped in 1.0.38. The old floor missed a ten-character password, so it was never masked.

items.title: config set cannot store a truthy string under a boolean key
items.detail: Shipped in 1.0.38. Covers every key whose shipped default is a boolean.

items.title: the doc-drift guard asserts facts, not remembered sentences
items.detail: Shipped in 1.0.38. It caught a stale line count within the hour of being written.

items.title: Ollama's context window is detected from /api/ps
items.detail: Shipped in 1.0.38. Verified against Ollama's documented reply; the failure mode is returning 0.

items.title: SGLang's context window is detected from /get_server_info
items.detail: On main, not in a release yet - so the anchor says untagged on purpose, and this suite fails the moment it becomes reachable from a tag without this line changing to match. That is the whole mechanism: 'unshipped' is a claim the repository can refuse.
